series: Climate Fiscal Policy Brief No. 6.5 · October 2026
title: The Macro-Fiscal-Energy Scenario Tool

slides.title: The Macro-Fiscal-Energy Scenario Tool
slides.subtitle: Financing and efficiency, not the size of the program, decide what climate investment does to growth and debt
slides.message: One open workbook for 186 countries runs the investment need, feasible carbon pricing, growth and the debt test in one pass. Financing and efficiency matter more than the program's size; for Kenya, carbon pricing on a clean grid pays for about 5 percent of the need.
slides.author: Stephen J. Stretton · writing in a personal capacity

slides.title: Ministries get four numbers on climate investment from four teams, and they rarely add up

slides.text: Each estimate needs the others: growth needs the financing, debt needs growth, carbon revenue depends on the emissions the investment avoids.

slides.title: For low-income borrowers, concessional finance changes the debt path, not the growth path
slides.note: GDP: % above baseline; debt: % of GDP, from 50 at the start (30 concessional, 20 commercial). Half of households hand-to-mouth; efficiency 0.6. The growth case rests on efficiency and the return on public capital.

slides.title: When generators' losses bind, a tax and a feebate cut emissions equally, but only the tax raises revenue
rows: Tax only, tariff rise capped at 2%
slides.note: Rebating to households would not raise the feasible price; compensating or retiring high-emitting plants would. If generators recover less of the carbon cost, the feasible tax falls to US$22.
slides.source: Working paper 6.5, Table 4; stylized power sector (2.Source/pricing_screen.py).
